screening.reason: Reports an ASD-vs-HC classification analysis on the ABIDE dataset with functional-connectivity findings (DMN/SMN/DAN/FPN), satisfying Inclusion 2-3, although ABIDE cohort size, pipeline and atlas are not explicitly reported (see charting notes)

evidence_spans.text:
Validation on two datasets, ADNI and ABIDE, demonstrates that DGCL surpasses traditional methods and other deep
learning models in predicting disease development stages.
evidence_spans.claim: The proposed diffusion-based graph contrastive learning model is validated on both ADNI and ABIDE for disease classification.

evidence_spans.text:
And the largest dataset for autism research comes
from Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange (ABIDE) [11].
evidence_spans.claim: ABIDE is used as the autism dataset in this study.

evidence_spans.text:
For ASD, the ROIs of the dataset can be divided into
eight functional subnetworks: cerebellum and subcortical
structure (CB), visual network (VN), somatic motor network
(SMN), dorsal attention network (DAN), ventral attention
network (VAN), edge network (LN), frontoparietal network
(FPN), and default mode network (DMN).
evidence_spans.claim: The ABIDE ROIs analysed for ASD are grouped into eight functional subnetworks.

evidence_spans.text:
Specifically,
the attention score in the SMN region is high, indicating that
connectivity plays a crucial role in ASD prediction in SMN.
evidence_spans.claim: Functional connectivity in the somatomotor network (SMN) was most important for predicting ASD.

evidence_spans.text:
In addition, attention scores were higher in the
DMN, DAN, and FPN regions (highlighted in the red box),
indicating that functional connectivity between DMN and
DAN, as well as between DMN and FPN, is also crucial for
predicting ASD
evidence_spans.claim: Functional connectivity involving the DMN, dorsal attention network and frontoparietal network also contributed strongly to ASD prediction.
On ABIDE, the proposed DGCL brain-network construction had higher reliability (ICC 0.71) and lower construction time than the PANDA baseline (ICC 0.64).

evidence_spans.text:
Five-fold 
cross-validation is used to evaluate the performance of the 
model.
evidence_spans.claim: Model performance was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation.

evidence_spans.text:
our work has two main limitations: one is that the proposed
model still cannot explain the pathogenesis of the detected
abnormal brain connections; the other is that the dataset
used in the current study is relatively small.
evidence_spans.claim: Authors note interpretability and small dataset size as limitations.

assessments.support: ABIDE is named as the autism dataset but no cohort N, sites, release (ABIDE I vs II), or exclusion/QC rule for the ABIDE subsample is reported in the available text (only ADNI's N=349 and Table 1 breakdown are given).

A detailed DTI/PANDA preprocessing pipeline and AAL-90 atlas are described for ADNI, and PANDA is also used as the comparison baseline for ABIDE (Table 6), but no equivalent preprocessing/atlas statement for the ABIDE data itself is given, and it is unclear whether ABIDE connectivity was derived from resting-state fMRI or structural data.
ASD vs HC label used; diagnostic instrument/source not stated anywhere in the available text.

Five-fold cross-validation is stated generically for "the model" but a full performance table (accuracy/AUC/sensitivity/specificity) is given only for the ADNI AD/NC/EMCI/LMCI classes (Table 5); no equivalent numeric ASD classification table is present in the extracted text, and no site-handling or leakage-control statement specific to ABIDE is given.

risk_of_bias.summary: ABIDE is used as a secondary validation dataset; the paper reports qualitative network findings (SMN, DMN, DAN, FPN implicated in ASD) and a reliability-metric table versus a PANDA baseline, but does not report the ABIDE cohort's N, sites, release, diagnosis source, preprocessing pipeline/atlas, or a numeric classification-performance table for ASD in the available text.

charting.title: A New Brain Network Construction Paradigm for Brain Disorder via Diffusion-Based Graph Contrastive Learning
charting.journal_conference: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
charting.disorder_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) vs Healthy Control (HC)
charting.data_types: functional connectivity (modality/resting-state status for the ABIDE subset not explicitly stated)
charting.feature_types: functional connectivity; brain network graphs over functional subnetworks (CB, VN, SMN, DAN, VAN, LN, FPN, DMN)
charting.specific_features: ROI-level attention scores over eight functional subnetworks; atlas/parcellation for the ABIDE experiment not explicitly stated (AAL-90 atlas is stated only for the ADNI/DTI experiment)
charting.feature_extraction_tools: PANDA toolbox used as the comparison baseline for brain-network construction on ABIDE; the proposed DGCL (diffusion-based brain-region alignment module + graph-contrastive brain-network optimization module) used as the main method; ABIDE-specific preprocessing pipeline not otherwise described
charting.importance_method: ROI attention/cue-vector scores from the learned brain-network matrix
charting.top_features_identified: Somatomotor network (SMN) connectivity, and DMN-DAN / DMN-FPN connectivity
charting.feature_change_direction: Higher attention/importance scores in SMN, DMN, DAN and FPN regions for ASD prediction (direction of connectivity change, e.g. hypo/hyperconnectivity, not stated)
charting.model_category: Diffusion-based generative brain-network construction (Dual U-Net denoising/registration) + graph convolutional network classifier with graph-contrastive brain-network optimization
charting.specific_algorithms: DGCL: Brain Region Alignment Module (BRAM, DDPM-based) and Brain Network Optimization Module (BNOM, GCN-based graph contrastive learning), compared against a PANDA-constructed network + GCN/MLP baseline
charting.validation_methodology: Five-fold cross-validation (stated generically for "the model"; no ABIDE-specific validation detail given)
charting.performance_metrics: Accuracy (ACC), sensitivity (SEN), specificity (SPE), AUC (metrics defined for the overall evaluation; ICC reliability also reported for ABIDE network construction)
charting.key_performance_results: No numeric ASD classification accuracy/AUC table is given in the extracted text (only qualitative statement that "the classification performance of the proposed model on two datasets is comprehensively better"); for ABIDE, network-construction reliability (ICC) was 0.71 for the proposed method versus 0.64 for PANDA
charting.summary_key_findings: On the ABIDE dataset, the proposed diffusion-based graph contrastive network identified SMN, DMN, DAN and FPN connectivity as most important for ASD prediction, and produced more reliable (higher ICC) and faster brain-network reconstructions than the PANDA toolbox; a quantitative ASD classification accuracy/AUC table analogous to the ADNI results is not present in the extracted text.
charting.features_associated_disorder: Functional connectivity in the somatomotor network (SMN); connectivity between DMN and DAN; connectivity between DMN and FPN
charting.future_directions_recommended: Plan to use other deep learning methods to analyze fMRI data and study brain function further; validate on larger datasets such as UK Biobank
charting.reviewer_notes: ABIDE release (I vs II), cohort N, sites, QC rule, diagnosis source, preprocessing pipeline and atlas are not explicitly reported in the extracted full text; disorder_cohort was defaulted to ABIDE I as the paper does not specify the release.

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (ASD vs HC); ABIDE used as a secondary validation dataset alongside ADNI; release, N and sites not reported in available text
narrative_row.methods: Diffusion-based generative brain-network construction (Brain Region Alignment Module, a DDPM-based registration network) combined with a graph-contrastive Brain Network Optimization Module (GCN-based), compared against brain networks built with the PANDA toolbox; five-fold cross-validation stated generically for the model.
narrative_row.outcomes: ROI attention scores identified somatomotor network (SMN) connectivity and DMN-DAN/DMN-FPN connectivity as most important for ASD prediction; on ABIDE the proposed method's constructed networks had higher reliability (ICC 0.71 vs 0.64) and much lower construction time than PANDA; no numeric ASD classification accuracy/AUC table is present in the extracted text.
narrative_row.key_limitations: ABIDE cohort N, sites, release, diagnosis source, preprocessing pipeline and atlas are not reported; no quantitative ASD classification performance table (unlike the detailed ADNI 5-fold results in Table 5); authors note the model cannot explain pathogenesis and the dataset used is relatively small.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Illustrates a predictive deep-learning paper where ABIDE is a secondary, thinly-documented validation dataset; useful as a negative example for cohort/pipeline reporting completeness in the knowledge graph.
